title: fix(plugin-detail): RelatedList's own filter box and sort read the masked stamp (objectui#10728)
body:
Fixes #10728

Clause-②: no

`RelatedList`'s own filter box and its own sort now read the `masked` stamp that `tableColumns` already puts on each column (PR objectui#10725, and since PR objectui#10819 also on every column withheld while the object's field types are unknown). A `password` / `secret` value no longer matches a typed term, and a masked column is no longer offered as a sort.

Branch `claude/issue-10728-related-list-masked-filter-sort`, base objectui `origin/main` `12809a5`, head `39831e7`. Implemented in session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01MCg3z5cGrV51xEddpGcxEY` for the PM claim `5858558615`.

## What changed (`@object-ui/plugin-detail`, `RelatedList.tsx`)

- **One derivation, `unmaskedColumnKeysKey`.** The keys of the columns handed to the table that do not carry `masked`, held as a content string (the `expandKey` / `selectKey` pattern, AGENTS.md commandment #10). The rule behind the stamp (`isMaskedDetailFieldType`, `objectTypesPending`) is not restated at the filter or the sort.
- **Filter box (`filterable`).** It swept `Object.values(row)`. It now sweeps the unmasked columns the list shows, reading the same raw values as before for those columns.
- **Sort.**
  - The `list` card's button row offers no button on a masked column.
  - `handleSort` (the button row's one door) and `handleTableSort` (the embedded table's `onSortChange`) refuse a masked key. The table already refuses a masked header itself; the list refuses it as well because in windowed mode the key becomes the server `$orderby`.
  - `sortedData` does not order by a key that is not an unmasked column, which covers a sort set before its column was stamped.
- **Hoist.** The filter / sort / pagination block (`filteredData` through `handleTableSort`) moved below `tableColumns` so it can read the stamp. Nothing between the old and new position read any of it, and no effect sits between them, so effect order is unchanged.
- JSDoc on the `filterable` and `sortable` props, the `filterActive` comment, the plugin-detail README (the "Not covered" sentence becomes a covered paragraph), and one stale comment in `RelatedList.sortDroppedOutsideWindowed.test.tsx`.
- Changeset `.changeset/10728-plugin-detail-related-list-masked-filter-sort.md` (`patch`). It names the pending `10657-plugin-detail-masked-related-list` changeset's "Also not covered" entry (the filter box and the `list` card's sort buttons) as no longer holding. That pending changeset is not edited.

## Zone 2 mechanism assumptions, measured

- **R1: confirmed.** `tableColumns` stamps `masked: true` when `objectTypesPending || isMaskedDetailFieldType(col.type, fieldDef?.type)`, and swaps in `withheldCell` while the types are unknown. Reading the stamp alone covers both cases; the pins below drive both.
- **R2: confirmed, and the list now follows the table's rule.** After PR objectui#10725, `data-table`'s own search filters `columns` through `isMaskedColumnKey`, so it sweeps the displayed columns minus the masked ones, never row keys that are not columns. The list's box swept every key on the row, so a hidden field that is no column at all (a declared `secret` the authored columns leave out, or an undeclared key the row carries) matched. The list now sweeps the unmasked displayed columns, the same rule.
  - **Narrowing, stated:** a term that matches only a field no column shows no longer keeps a row. Said in the changeset and the README. Pinned as its own case.
- **R3: confirmed.** `filteredData` / `sortedData` were computed before `tableColumns`. The block was moved below it; there is still one stamping pass.
- **R4: measured.**
  - The sort state is never persisted: `sortField` is component state, set only by `handleSort` and `handleTableSort`. Both now refuse a masked key.
  - An authored initial sort CAN name a masked column today, through `defaultSort` (what `record:related_list` passes its `sort` as). In client mode it never orders the rows (`sortedData` reads `sortField` only). In windowed mode it goes out as the server `$orderby` whenever no user sort is set (the existing `RelatedList.sortDroppedOutsideWindowed` CONTROL case pins that path). The platform's sortability projection documents that `secret` and the other masked types keep `sortable: true` because neither runtime door refuses an ORDER BY over them. So the server orders a paged list by the hidden value.
  - **Not changed here, on purpose.** Deciding it at the fetch would need the verdict before the columns exist. The columns derive from the rows the fetch returns. And a sort on a field no column shows (`-created_at`) is legitimate, so "not an unmasked column" cannot be the test there; it would take a restated type rule. The spec text says refusing such a sort is a runtime-door decision first. Listed under Acceptance notes and in the report as a finding for the seat.

## Design choices

- **Fail closed for a sort key that names no column**, as `data-table`'s `isMaskedColumnKey` does. In client mode a sort on a column that later drops out of the list (the permission answer landing, or the derived walk's column cap moving) stops ordering the rows. Windowed mode is unchanged there: its order is the server's, and `sortedData` does not re-sort a window.
- **The withheld window costs what PR objectui#10725 already stated for the table**: while the definition is loading, or after its read failed, the box keeps no row for any term and no sort button is offered.

## Evidence

New pins: `packages/plugin-detail/src/__tests__/RelatedList.maskedFilterSort-10728.test.tsx`, 12 cases. The real renderers draw the table; a `SchemaRenderer` wrapper only records the view schema. Every absence is read after a control in the same mounted tree has answered.

- filter, three column shapes (bare strings, authored objects, the derived walk): the term `ZULU` (in `api_key` `RAW-ZULU-10728`) and `TOKEN-B` (a `secret`) keep no row; the name terms `Ada` / `Cyd` keep their row (control);
- filter narrowing: `ECHO` (an undeclared key on the row) and `TOKEN-C` (a declared `secret` the authored columns omit) keep no row; `Bob` keeps its row (control);
- filter, withheld window: `ZULU` and `Ada` keep no row; once the definition lands `Ada` keeps its row (control) and `ZULU` still keeps none;
- `list` card, three shapes: no button on `API Key` / `Token`; the `Name` button sorts (control, desc order `Cyd, Bob, Ada`);
- `list` card, withheld window: no sort button at all; once the definition lands, exactly `Name` (control). Buttons are found by their `lucide-arrow-up-down` glyph, not by label: before the definition lands a bare-string column's header is not its declared label, and the first version of this case read an empty row on base for that reason. The ablation below was re-run after that repair;
- a sort set before its column was stamped (the author re-types `code` as `password`), on the `list` card and through the table's `onSortChange`: the rows return to their incoming order after the control sort ordered them;
- windowed: the table asking to sort by `api_key` sends no `$orderby` naming it; `name desc` reaches the server (control).

**Ablation (red on base).** With the fix committed, `RelatedList.tsx` was replaced by its base blob (`git show 12809a5:…`). The on-disk hash equalled the base blob (`5b238d3`), with `unmaskedColumnKeysKey` count 0 and the `Object.values(row)` count 1 read from the file. Run under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` restore: `Tests 12 failed (12)`. Every case failed on its subject assertion, never on a CONTROL, for example `the password value is not searched: expected [ 'Ada' ] to deeply equal []`, `every column is withheld: expected [ 'name', 'api_key' ] to deeply equal []`, `the masked key is never sent as $orderby: expected [ 'api_key' ] to not include 'api_key'`. Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABS_PATH`. The hash equalled the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` was 0 bytes.

## Gates, at `39831e7`

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-detail/`: `Test Files 216 passed | 1 skipped (217)`, `Tests 2120 passed | 8 skipped (2128)`, exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail type-check` (echoes `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`): exit 0, after `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/plugin-detail^...'` (`Tasks: 11 successful, 11 total`). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists the new test file.
- eslint on the three changed `.ts`/`.tsx` files (the package's own `eslint .` config, `--format json`): 3 files in the report, 0 errors. `RelatedList.tsx` has 75 warnings, the same count and rule mix as its base blob. Population: `--print-config` resolves a config for each. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), and no local rule reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move a verdict in an untouched file. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-test-path-roots`: all exit 0. `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the five paths answers NOT GOVERNED.
- NOT MEASURED: `check-readme-exports`, reason: it needs every package's `dist` type entry (prerequisite not met in this worktree). The README hunk adds no fenced block and no import.

## Acceptance notes

- **Residual (windowed, stale key):** the fetch effect is declared before `tableColumns`, so a user sort set on a column that later becomes masked (its authored `columns` re-typed, or `api` switching objects while mounted) is still sent as `$orderby`. Both setters refuse a masked key, so this needs the stamp to arrive after the sort; `record:related_list` authors static columns per node.
- **Authored `sort` on a masked field** (R4 above): a paged list is ordered server-side by the hidden value. Reported to the seat as a same-family finding; not changed here.
- **`type: 'list'` renders no rows.** `RelatedList` hands `{ type: 'data-list' }` to `SchemaRenderer`, and no renderer registers `data-list`, so the card draws `Unknown component type: data-list` (seen in this PR's test DOM). The in-repo producer (`record:related_list`) renders `type="table"`. A `related-list` node cannot carry the list variant either, since its `type` key is the registry key. So the `list` card, and its sort buttons, are reached only by a direct React consumer of the exported component. Noted, not filed; no carrier.
